source.text:
> I really don't understand the sentiment. If AI would in any way turn out to be too smart or dangerous, "we" would just switch of the power in the datacenter where this happened. Or all the datacenters.

Just like we did with all the carbon-dioxide emitting fossil fuel plants?

Or the carcinogenic cigarettes?

How long did it take us to stop putting lead in petrol?

Also, the point of AI smarts being a risk is that it either convinces us to not do that, perhaps by making itself indispensable, perhaps just by being persuasive, or perhaps hiding its own danger until too late.

(Edit: just to add one point here: on persuasive, look at how many people have "AI psychosis" and similar, look at how many CEOs are eager to demand AI's use in the workforce. Persuasive can happen even when it's not competent).

> The "Skynet" scenario only works if "the ai" had infected everything

That would be the Terminator 3 Skynet. Terminator 1 did that with just military control.

> on the world without anyone noticing AND has the ability to generate power for itself AND be able to build gpus AND be able to build all the other infrastructure without any human help.

Everyone can notice, so long as we don't all act the right way, c.f. climate change. Or, not that fiction is evidence of anything beyond the culture in which it arose, Terminator 3, where noticing and responding the wrong way was the final act which gave it military control.

Also, nothing requires an AI to survive wiping out humanity. Cancers don't stop just because it will kill the host and themselves with it.

> We are very far away from all these circumstances, are we not?

We don't know how far we are from that; but we can point to a trillionaire who argued before his shareholders that he was going to build a "robot army" that he wanted "influence" over, which he has stated in public will outnumber humanity.

His other business marketed itself in its IPO on the basis of building space-based data centres, and a moon factory which would use full automation to, each year, produce new PV and compute that's order-of 30x humanity's current total global electrical power output.

I would very much like to hope everything from Musk that I just retold is all a scam. If it isn't a scam, even just building that much and putting it in LEO has more impact on our climate than all greenhouse gasses to date, even without any actual offensive action.

Likewise, I would very much like to hope that everyone worried about this has over-generalised from limited domains of success. If it isn't, if the generalisation is valid, then yes, the AI will (soonish) be able to not only design their own power and GPU and robot bodies, but also control those bodies to mine the raw minerals and refine them and make all the things they need.
